docs.title: CAS chaos eases? Jefferies names top stock picks as options volumes recover, IPOs and commodities gain tra
docs.text:
The impact of the recently introduced closing auction session ( CAS ) may finally be easing on Dalal Street, with issues around the new mechanism appearing to settle, Jefferies said in its latest report. The brokerage noted that options volumes improved in September after a sharp drop in August.
 The international brokerage said industry-wide September index options premium ADTO stood at Rs 68,100 crore, broadly similar to July levels before CAS was introduced on August 3. The new mechanism changed how closing prices are calculated for stocks in the futures and options (F&O) segment.
Jefferies said the recovery to pre-CAS levels was largely driven by easing CAS-related issues and a spike in the VIX.
 Also read | Stocks to buy: Jefferies remains bullish on these 4 capital market stocks, sees up to 36% upside 
 Jefferies on BSE and MCX
BSE’s ADTO in September increased 24% from the previous month to Rs 23,200 crore. BSE’s options market share fell slightly to 34.1% from 34.7% last month, as NSE had an additional expiry, Jefferies noted. It also highlighted that BSE’s cash-market share rose to 8.8% in September, marking the third consecutive monthly increase, led by the mega NSE IPO.
 Live Events
MCX, meanwhile, saw options ADTO rise 21% month-on-month, while futures ADTO fell 7% MoM. Jefferies noted that the increase in options ADTO was led by a 44% MoM rise in energy options ADTO. The commodity exchange is among the international brokerage’s top capital-market picks.
 Jefferies on Groww share price
Groww could benefit from a recovery in orders, a pick-up in its MTF book and a rise in commodity trading in September, Jefferies said. Groww’s MTF book, which had plateaued in August, rose 10% month-on-month to Rs 4,300 crore in September. Commodity turnover on Groww’s platform in the second quarter of FY27 also jumped 26% sequentially.
Large AMCs, excluding Nippon Life India Asset Management, lost equity AUM market share in September, while AMCs outside the top five saw their share of schemes among the top 15 equity schemes rise, Jefferies pointed out. For depositories, delivered quantities, IPOs and demat openings have been improving. The brokerage named Groww, MCX, KFIN and Nuvama as its top picks.

docs.title: Semiconductor push, govt support driving EMS sector's growth, but valuation a concern: How 3 stocks with most buy calls are placed
docs.text:
Synopsis
 Investor enthusiasm around the sector is visible in the performance of nine EMS stocks covered by multiple brokerages. The group has delivered an equal weighted average return of 55.3% so far in 2026, compared with 1.1% for the Nifty 500 Equal Weighted Index. Seven of the nine stocks have delivered posi tive returns, while three have gained over 100%. The analysis is based on closing prices as of 28 September 2026.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 India’s electronic manufacturing services (EMS) sector is growing at a healthy pace, supported by rising demand for electronics and strong orders from sectors such as defence, aerospace, artificial intelligence (AI), automobiles, electric vehicles and clean energy. According to KPMG, one of the Big Four accounting firms, the Indian EMS industry has expanded from $10-12 billion in FY2019-20 to $40-45 billion in FY2024-25.
Yet, India accounts for just 5-6% of the global EMS market, leaving room for growth. The share is expected to rise over the coming decade, with KPMG projecting the Indian EMS industry to cross $150 billion by FY2029-30.
Growing export opportunities, the China-plus-one strategy, which involves companies diversifying their supply chains beyond China, and government support are some of the other key tailwinds. At the same time, domestic EMS companies are gradually moving beyond basic assembly to more complex, higher-value products, opening another avenue for growth. 
Investor enthusiasm around the sector is visible in the performance of nine EMS stocks covered by multiple brokerages. The group has delivered an equal-weighted average return of 55.3% so far in 2026, compared with 1.1% for the Nifty 500 Equal Weighted Index. Seven of the nine stocks have delivered positive returns, while three have gained over 100%. The analysis is based on closing prices as of 28 September 2026.
 Share of global EMS market in 2025 
 Asia Pacific accounts for more than half of the global EMS market. 
 Government support
Government policies have played an important role in the sector’s growth. Initiatives such as Make in India and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes have encouraged domestic manufacturing across segments including mobile phones, electronics, white goods, IT hardware and telecom equipment. The Electronic Component Manufacturing Scheme complements these initiatives by encouraging local production of critical components such as printed circuit boards, camera modules and display modules.
 Semiconductor push
The government’s semiconductor push could provide the next leg of growth for the electronics manufacturing ecosystem. While India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 1.0 focused on laying the foundation for semiconductor manufacturing, the recently approved ISM 2.0, or Semicon 2.0, aims to deepen the country’s semiconductor design and manufacturing capabilities. With a budgetary outlay of Rs.1.27 trillion, the programme will focus on semiconductor design, equipment, fabrication, advanced packaging, and research and development.
For EMS companies, greater availability of domestically manufactured semiconductors could strengthen supply chains, reduce dependence on imports and provide opportunities to move further up the value chain. Experts therefore see Semicon 2.0 as an important step in widening opportunities for Indian EMS players.

Raghavan Viswanathan, Partner, Deal Advisory, KPMG in India, says ISM 2.0 is aimed at long-term value creation and greater semiconductor self-reliance. “ISM 1.0 and 2.0, and possibly a future 3.0, could help make the 2030s India’s decade for semiconductors,” he says.
 Complexity, a growth driver
Another important shift is taking place within the EMS industry itself. As large original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) increasingly outsource manufacturing, domestic EMS companies are moving towards more complex applications. These require stronger engineering capabilities, certifications, testing, reliability and system-integration expertise.
A recent Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) report argues that complexity, rather than scale alone, is becoming a key differentiator in the EMS business. As OEMs outsource more technically demanding products to specialised manufacturing partners, the addressable market for Indian EMS companies could expand. Greater complexity can also improve customer stickiness and provide EMS companies with a longer runway for growth.
Vinay Jain, Head of Research & Fund Manager at Karma Capital, remains positive on the long-term opportunity and believes the EMS story in India is changing. Companies are moving beyond simple assembly and printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) towards box builds, system integration, precision engineering and more complex electronics. In other words, the sector is gradually evolving from a capacity-led story to a capability-led one.
 ALSO READ | AI can pick the fund, but can it stop you from selling at the bottom? 
The shift towards higher-value products could also help margins. Analysts see scope for operating margin improvement as the product mix shifts toward areas such as automotive, industrial and defence electronics. Companies could also benefit from operating leverage as higher utilisation spreads fixed costs over a larger revenue base.
 Premium valuations
The sharp rally in EMS stocks, however, has also pushed valuations higher. According to Bloomberg data, the historical price-to-earnings ratios of the nine EMS companies range from 50 to 138 times. Five of the nine are trading at a premium of more than 20% to their respective five-year average valuations.
“Valuations are split, and investors should pay only for genuine depth of manufacturing,” says Manish Bhandari, CEO and Portfolio Manager, Vallum Capital.

docs.title: France's Schneider Electric nears $20 billion deal to buy US software group PTC: Report
docs.text:
France's Schneider Electric is nearing a deal to buy US software group PTC for about $20 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday citing people with knowledge of the matter.
 A deal may be announced as soon as Monday, the newspaper said, adding that discussions between the two companies were ongoing and there was no certainty they would result in a deal.
Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. Schneider Electric and PTC did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment outside regular business hours. 
Boston-based PTC has a market value of $15.63 billion, according to LSEG data.
In July, the company had lifted its annual revenue forecast after third-quarter results, betting on strong demand for its core industrial software and artificial intelligence-powered tools.

 On the BSE, it opened at Rs 28.30, a discount of 11.56% to the issue price.
The Rs 420-crore public issue was priced in the range of Rs 30–32 per share, with the upper end of the price band at Rs 32. The issue comprised a fresh issue of 8.97 crore shares aggregating to Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 4.16 crore shares worth Rs 133 crore.

The remaining proceeds will be utilised for inorganic growth through acquisitions and general corporate purposes. The total amount earmarked under the specified IPO objects is Rs 182 crore.
 Financial Performance
Acevector Ltd.’s total income increased 32%, rising from Rs 407 crore in FY25 to Rs 538 crore in FY26. Meanwhile, the company narrowed its net loss significantly to Rs 45 crore in FY26, from Rs 126 crore in FY25.
 About Acevector Ltd.
Incorporated in 2007, Acevector Ltd. operates an asset-light digital commerce ecosystem through its subsidiaries, spanning data, technology, and AI-driven businesses. Its operations include a value-focused e-commerce marketplace, e-commerce enablement SaaS platforms, and consumer brand businesses.
The ecosystem comprises: (i) Snapdeal, a value-driven lifestyle e-commerce marketplace offering affordable and quality merchandise across lifestyle categories (ii) Uniware, Convertway, and Shipway, providing a comprehensive suite of e-commerce enablement SaaS products that support end-to-end e-commerce operations; and (iii) Stellaro Brands, an omnichannel portfolio of value-focused consumer brands. In FY 2026, Snapdeal served customers nation-wide across 18,972 pin codes in India, primarily catering to middle-income, value-conscious consumers in Tier 2+ and smaller cities—an important segment of the large untapped value e-commerce market.

docs.title: US stocks enter seasonally strong Q4 with bond yields, AI spending in focus
docs.text:
US stocks are entering the fourth quarter with historically favourable seasonal trends, but rising bond yields , elevated market valuations and growing dependence on massive artificial intelligence spending could challenge further gains, according to a report by Reuters.
 The benchmark S&P 500 had gained nearly 13% in 2026 through Friday and was about 1% below its record high reached in mid-August, according to Reuters. Investors now face a packed final quarter, with the third-quarter earnings season, a key Federal Reserve meeting and the November 3 US midterm elections all likely to influence market direction.
 As on 03 Oct 2026, 01:30 AM IST
 S&P 500 Top Gainers
 Synopsys 489.90 (18.02%) 
 Hewlett Packard 69.35 (12.76%) 
 Accenture 198.99 (12.23%) 
 ON Semiconductor 84.89 (11.77%) 
 Gainers » 
 S&P 500 Top Losers
 Corteva 11.92 (-84.69%) 
 AppLovin 268.22 (-12.25%) 
 Coterra Energy 32.56 (-8.62%) 
 Western Digital 415.29 (-8.42%) 
 Losers » 
 Also Read | Global Market Today: Asian shares rise as Fed hike bets ease, oil gains 
 Q4 historically strong for stocks
The fourth quarter has traditionally been the strongest period of the year for US equities. Since 1945, the S&P 500 has posted an average gain of 4.2% during the October-December period and finished higher in 85% of those quarters, according to research firm CFRA, Reuters reported.
Fourth quarters during midterm election years have been even stronger, with the S&P 500 averaging a 6.4% gain as investors typically get greater clarity on the political outlook after the elections.
 Live Events
However, the broader history of midterm years is less encouraging. The S&P 500 has historically experienced an average decline of about 15% during midterm years, according to Wells Fargo Investment Institute, Reuters reported. The index's deepest decline so far in 2026 has been about 9%, leaving investors alert to the possibility of a correction before the election.
A significant shift in control of Congress could also introduce uncertainty around US policy and create pressure on equities, Reuters reported. At the same time, any election-related pullback could potentially create an opportunity for investors to add to positions.
 Also Read | Nasdaq rises 1%, Dow, S&P close higher as weak jobs data tempers rate hike bets 
 Rising Treasury yields emerge as key threat
The biggest immediate challenge for equities is the sharp rise in bond yields. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to 5.34% last week, its highest level in 24 years.
Higher yields can make bonds more attractive relative to stocks while also putting pressure on equity valuations. They can raise borrowing costs for companies and consumers, potentially weighing on economic activity and corporate investment.
The report by Reuters stated that the recent rise in yields has been driven by expectations for strong economic growth, higher energy costs that could keep inflation elevated and increased demand for capital as companies raise funds for artificial intelligence-related expansion.
The Federal Reserve's policy outlook will remain closely watched. Minutes from the central bank's latest meeting are due on Wednesday and could provide clues about the path of interest rates, including the possibility of another rate increase later this year.
Following weaker-than-expected US jobs data released on Friday, markets continued to expect the Fed to avoid another immediate rate increase at its upcoming meeting, the report stated.
 Earnings expectations set a high bar
The third-quarter earnings season will provide another major test for equities. PepsiCo and Delta Air Lines are among the large companies scheduled to report results this week, with major US banks expected to begin reporting shortly afterward.
Corporate earnings have exceeded already-high expectations this year, helping support the stock market's gains. That strong performance, however, has also raised expectations for the upcoming results.
S&P 500 companies are expected to report earnings growth of more than 30% in the third quarter from a year earlier, according to LSEG IBES data cited by Reuters.
 AI spending becomes critical market driver
Investors will be particularly focused on spending plans by major technology companies as they assess whether the huge investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure can continue to support earnings growth.
AI hyperscalers have committed enormous sums to data centres, computing infrastructure and related technology, benefiting semiconductor companies, equipment makers and other parts of the technology supply chain.
The US stock market's performance has become closely tied to the AI theme, making capital expenditure plans from major hyperscalers a key focus of the upcoming earnings season.
Any upward revisions to AI-related capital spending could reinforce the market's bullish narrative. Conversely, signs that companies are becoming more cautious about investment could raise concerns about whether the AI-driven rally can continue at its current pace.
With the S&P 500 already sitting near record highs, investors therefore enter the traditionally strong fourth quarter facing a delicate balance between favourable seasonality and a series of significant macroeconomic and market risks.

docs.text:
Mumbai: KKR-owned Healthium Medtech and Temasek-backed Romsons Group are the major contenders to acquire an about 70-80% stake in Delhi-based medical devices manufacturer and distributor BL Lifesciences , said people aware of the development.
 The company is likely to be valued ₹1,800-2,000 crore, the people said. KPMG is advising the promoters on the stake sale. BL Lifesciences, a fourth-generation family-owned business, primarily focuses on products for cardiac surgery, critical care, interventional cardiology, anaesthesia and surgical care.

Its portfolio spans perfusion systems such as heart-lung packs, oxygenators, cardioplegia sets; cath-lab kits, central venous catheters; invasive pressure-monitoring systems; and a broad range of surgical consumables including blood bags, instruments and wound-care products.
KKR and Temasek spokespersons declined to comment. An email sent to BL Lifesciences managing director Sunil Aggarwal did not elicit any responses till press time Monday.
 Live Events
KKR acquired Healthium in 2024 for ₹7,000 crore, outbidding a consortium of Mankind Pharma, ChrysCapital and Novo Holdings.

Expectations of robust corporate earnings have helped US equities outperform global peers over the past six months despite geopolitical uncertainty and persistent inflation concerns.

“Many investors expect higher yields to derail the equity rally, but I think the market still has enough momentum to push through further increases in interest rates,” Peter Andersen, founder of Andersen Capital Management, told Reuters.

Brent crude futures hovered near the psychologically important $ 100 per barrel level as concerns about disruptions to Gulf oil infrastructure persisted amid the Middle East conflict.

docs.title: Yes Bank shares rise 3% after Q2 business update shows loans surging 24% YoY, deposits up 20%
docs.text:
Shares of Yes Bank gained 3% to Rs 21.22 on the BSE on Monday after the private lender released its provisional business update for the July-September quarter of the ongoing financial year 2027, reporting a nearly 24% surge in loans and advances, while deposits grew around 20% during the period.
 The company on Sunday reported that its loans and advances stood at around Rs 3.1 lakh crore at the end of the second quarter of FY27, marking 23.8% year-on-year growth from the Rs 2.5 lakh crore loan book reported in the same period of FY26, and 8.6% sequential rise from the Rs 2.85 crore reported in the first quarter of the ongoing financial year 2027.
 Also read | RBI could keep rates higher for longer amid global and local risks 
 Yes Bank's deposits rise 20% YoY to Rs 3.5 lakh crore
Yes Bank’s deposits meanwhile rose 19.5% YoY to Rs 3.54 lakh crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2.96 lakh crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Sequentially, the private lender’s deposits grew 12.3% quarter on quarter from Rs 3.15 lakh crore reported in Q1 FY27. Deposits growth normalised for FCNR(B) stood at 6.5% YoY and 13.2% QoQ. CASA deposits rose around 7% YoY to Rs 1.06 lakh crore.
The bank’s CASA ratio stood at 30% in Q2 FY27, as against 33.7% in Q2 FY26 and 32.7% in Q1 FY27. Normalised for the special RBI scheme, its CASA ratio stood at 31.7% during the second quarter of FY27. Its Credit to Deposit Ratio rose slightly YoY to 87.5% during the quarter under review from 84.5% in the same period last year, although it contracted from 90.4% reported in the quarter which ended on June 30, 2026.
 Live Events
 Yes Bank share price
 Yes Bank shares have fallen over 2% in a week and 8% in a month, amid an overall decline in the stock market. The shares of the private lender have dropped more than 3% in 2026 so far, outperforming the broader Nifty Bank index which has tumbled around 9% at the same time, driven by multiple headwinds.
In the longer term, Yes Bank shares have delivered around 21% returns over three years and more than 58% in five years. The company has a market capitalisation of more than Rs 65,130 crore.

docs.title: Why US Treasury bond yields matter, what it means for Indian investors, and the impact on rupee
docs.text:
Synopsis
 Cutting through money jargon, one topic at a time. This week, Sanket Dhanorkar explains why yields on US Treasury bonds matter, and what it means for Indian investors. Rising US bond yields mean investors are demanding a higher return to buy and hold that debt. This reflects concerns over the weak fiscal position of the US and the inflationary impact from steep oil prices.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 United States Treasury yields have risen to multi-year highs. The yield on 10-year US Treasuries has climbed to 5.34% (intra-day), surpassing its 2007 peak, and hitting its highest since early 2002. The 30-year yield has touched 5.6%, also not seen since 2002. This sharp rise in US Treasury yields has sent shockwaves through global markets, including India.
 What is driving up the yield
Rising US bond yields mean investors are demanding a higher return to buy and hold that debt. This reflects concerns over the weak fiscal position of the US and the inflationary impact from steep oil prices. Investors anticipate rising government borrowing to meet the growing fiscal deficit, which will bring large supply of fresh bonds to the market. This excess supply pulls down bond prices, putting upward pressure on bond yields.
 The US Federal Reserve, the country’s central bank, also raised its policy rate by 25 basis points (bps) in September to 3.75-4%. With rising oil prices feeding into inflation, expectations are that the Fed may need to keep interest rates higher for longer. Stronger-than-expected US economic activity also makes it less likely that inflation will ease any time soon, and is keeping bond yields buoyant. Besides, competition for capital from the private sector to fund heavy investments into artificial intelligence infrastructure is keeping yields bubbling. 
 How it affects markets
US bonds are perceived as the world’s safest and most liquid assets. They effectively set the price of money across the world.
A higher US Treasury yield raises the return available on dollar assets. This sets a high bar for return from other assets. Investors reassess the returns they require from other assets, including emerging-market bonds and equities. These assets must offer enough additional return over a US Treasury to compensate for the extra risks of holding an emerging-market asset, including currency risk. If they cannot, global investors may reassess allocations to emerging-market equities and bonds. This affects the flow of foreign capital to countries like India.
US yields are rising even as Indian bond yields have stayed relatively stable. This has narrowed the India-US bond yield gap to historic lows. A narrower spread makes it less attractive for global investors to hold rupee-denominated bonds, after accounting for currency risk.
Rising US bond yields also complicate the Reserve Bank of India’s policy choices. They make it more difficult for the central bank to consider rate cuts, even if domestic inflation is lower. While the Indian banking regulator may not follow the Fed in hiking rates, its freedom to pursue an independent monetary policy gets squeezed.
 Impact on rupee
US bond yields are rising at a time when the rupee is already under pressure. If demand for dollars rises or capital flows out, emerging-market currencies, including the rupee, can come under pressure. India’s dependence on crude oil imports make this a particularly challenging situation. Every dollar of oil becomes more expensive in rupee terms when the currency weakens. When price of crude oil itself is rising, the added burden of weaker rupee makes imports even more expensive, stoking inflation.

docs.text:
Japan’s Nikkei share average rose more than 2% on Monday to a three-month high, driven by gains in artificial intelligence-related stocks following a rally on Wall Street at the end of last week.
 The Nikkei rose 2.53% to 70,037.61 by the midday break, its highest level since early July, as per a report by Reuters. The broader Topix gained 1.16% to 4,138.57.
 As on 03 Oct 2026, 01:30 AM IST

 Gainers »

 Corteva 11.92 (-84.69%)

 Losers » 
 Also Read | Global Market Today: Asian shares rise as Fed hike bets ease, oil gains 
Investors bought AI-related stocks, although market sentiment remained more subdued than earlier in the year when the Nikkei hit a record high, Reuters reported, citing Mamoru Shimode, chief strategist at Resona Asset Management. Shimode said the AI rally was likely to continue, but investors would become more selective.
U.S. stocks advanced on Friday after weaker-than-expected jobs data reduced expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike at its policy meeting this month.
 Live Events
In Japan, chip-related stocks led Monday’s gains. Advantest and Tokyo Electron climbed 4.5% and 5.7%, respectively, providing the biggest boosts to the Nikkei. Technology investor SoftBank Group rose 3.68%.
Memory-chip maker Kioxia edged up 0.49%. Its shares remain nearly 50% below the record high reached in mid-June.
 Also Read | Nasdaq rises 1%, Dow, S&P close higher as weak jobs data tempers rate hike bets 
Kioxia’s limited gain reflected a balance between buying interest and selling by investors looking to reduce losses as the stock rose, Shimode told Reuters.
Bank stocks also advanced, with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group gaining 0.99% and Mizuho Financial Group rising 1.86%.
The Topix growth share index rose 1.46%, while the value share index gained 0.89%.
Of more than 1,500 stocks on the Tokyo Stock Exchange ’s Prime Market, 53% rose, 42% fell and 3% were unchanged.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

Reliance Power 's board of directors on Monday approved the issuance of up to 46.20 crore equity shares/warrants worth Rs 1,525 crore via preferential allotment mode.
 The board has set the issue price at Rs 33 per share.
The issue price of equity shares/warrants is at a discount of 13% over Monday's closing price of Rs 38.15 on the NSE. The announcement was made after market hours and Reliance Power shares on Monday ended with gains of Rs 1.81 or 4.98% over the previous closing price.
 Reliance Infrastructure Limited, the promoter of the company, will enhance its equity stake by over Rs 600 crore, a company filing said. The other investors in the preferential issue are Authum Investment and Infrastructure Limited and Sanatan Financial Advisory Services Private Limited.
The proceeds from the preferential issue will be utilised to expand business operations directly and/or through investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures, debt reduction and for general corporate purposes, the filing said.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.

HDFC Bank shares ended sharply lower on Monday, reversing an early rally as investors appeared to pare their initial positive reaction to clarity on the bank's leadership transition and a strong Q2 business update.
The stock had opened 1.67% higher at Rs 733.25 but quickly reversed gains and slipped into the red. HDFC Bank shares closed at Rs 704.80, down 2.27%.
The early rally came after the Reserve Bank of India approved Anup Bagchi's appointment as HDFC Bank's new MD & CEO for a three-year term starting October 27. He will succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose term ends on October 26.
Bagchi, who has spent 34 years with the ICICI Group, has held leadership roles across banking, insurance, capital markets, treasury and wealth management. His appointment brings an end to uncertainty around HDFC Bank's leadership succession and comes as the lender works to improve growth, margins and investor confidence.
Motilal Oswal retained its 'Buy' rating on the stock with a target price of Rs925. The brokerage said Bagchi's appointment "removes a key overhang surrounding HDFC Bank 's leadership succession and brings an external perspective at a time when the bank is seeking to rebuild investor confidence."
The brokerage expects HDFC Bank's operating performance to improve from FY28E, supported by a recovery in loan growth and margins. It expects loans to grow at a 14% CAGR over FY26-28E and PAT growth to recover to 13% YoY by FY28E.
PL India also retained its 'BUY' rating with a target price of Rs950. "Given his strong pedigree, we view Mr. Bagchi's appointment positively," the brokerage said, while flagging LDR, NIM and the gap between management guidance and execution as key issues for the new leadership to address.
HDFC Bank's Q2 business update showed gross advances rising 16.3% YoY and 5.2% QoQ to Rs32.19 lakh crore. AUM increased 15.3% YoY and 5.8% QoQ to Rs33.07 lakh crore.
Deposits grew 18.8% YoY and 4.9% QoQ to Rs33.27 lakh crore, while CASA deposits rose 10.8% YoY and 2.6% QoQ to Rs10.52 lakh crore.
The strong deposit and loan growth comes ahead of Bagchi taking charge and gives the incoming leadership a stronger operating base as it looks to address HDFC Bank's CASA ratio, NIMs, credit growth and merger synergies.
According to CNBC-TV18 sources, HDFC Bank's strategy under the new leadership will focus on three broad areas - rebuilding brand and trust, balance-sheet optimisation and future readiness. The bank is also expected to sharpen its focus on technology, digitisation and customer service, while improving agility and alignment across teams.

 Brokerages yet to revise price targets on HDFC Bank despite CEO appointment 
 Street remains positive on the stock, with 47 analysts polled on Bloomberg retaining the ‘buy’ calls on the stock. 
 Archishma Iyer 
 October 05, 2026 / 13:59 IST 
 --> 
 HDFC Bank 
 Brokerages maintain buy ratings on HDFC Bank.
 Street awaits Q2 results after CEO change.
 Bagchi's appointment aims to boost confidence.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Brokerages are yet to revise their expectations on HDFC Bank despite the appointment of a new CEO, suggesting that the Street is still digesting Anup Bagchi’s appointment while investors could await the bank’s second-quarter results for any incremental revisions.
An analysis based on analysts polled on Bloomberg reveals that the Street’s consensus has remained the same, with 47 ‘buy’ calls and two ‘hold’ calls, and no sell calls on the stock.
Nonetheless, the Street seems optimistic on Bagchi’s appointment.
“We believe the appointment should help restore investor and customer confidence in the bank, given that Bagchi is a banking veteran with experience across diverse responsibilities within the ICICI Bank group,” say analysts at Emkay Global Financial Services.
“His non-obtrusive leadership style, focus on broader strategic priorities, and aversion to micromanagement should help him carry the core team along, although some churn at the senior management level is possible". The brokerage has maintained its ‘buy’ call on the stock with a target price of Rs 1,225 apiece
Other brokerages such as Morgan Stanley and Kotak Institutional Equities have also maintained their ‘buy’ rating on the stock, with the latter saying that faster growth may follow balance-sheet optimisation and a re-rating of the stock could happen gradually.
Both have maintained a target price of Rs 1,025 and Rs 1,050 apiece, respectively.
However, while the HDFC Bank stock opened the day's trade positively, up 1.5 percent, it pared its gains to trade more than 2 percent lower at Rs 705.25 per share at Rs 1340 IST.
Analysts say they would wait for incremental triggers for re-rating and that September Fy27 quarter results could give them some room to relook at their target prices. The management's outlook, more so from Anup Bagchi, the new CEO succeeding Sashidhar Jagdishan, if he joins the investor call on October 17, on factors such as net interest margin trajectory, merger synergies, and CASA ratio improvement, would be closely tracked by the street.
These aspects could potentially lead to a re-rating of the stock, according to analysts.
The bank’s NIM has remained below 3 percent since the second quarter of FY24, following the merger with HDFC Ltd. Analysts have been expecting margins to recover as the impact of the higher-cost liabilities inherited from the mortgage lender gradually fades.
One of the key areas the Street will watch is whether HDFC Bank can accelerate loan growth without putting further pressure on its funding profile. The bank has been trying to rebalance its balance sheet after the merger, while also improving its deposit mobilisation and reducing its dependence on bulk deposits.
“The merger substantially enhanced HDFC Bank's mortgage and customer franchise, but the bank has yet to fully demonstrate the operating leverage and cross-selling benefits that investors had initially expected. Bagchi's experience could potentially help accelerate cross-selling across the bank’s large customer base and improve customer-level economics,” Motilal Oswal analysts said.

Shares of HDFC Bank gave up early gains to close over 2% lower on October 5 as investors weighed the impact of Anup Bagchi's appointment as CEO at India's biggest private lender.
The veteran banker, the first outsider to lead the Mumbai-based bank, succeeds Sashidhar Jagdishan, who decided not to seek reappointment after his second three-year term ends in late October. Bagchi pipped insider and Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha, who was also among the contenders for the post.
 HDFC shares , which have the largest weight on Nifty 50 benchmark index, closed 2.3% lower at Rs 704.8 apiece, wiping off Rs 25,258 crore in market capitalisation, while the benchmark rose 0.6%. The stock had risen about 1.8% in early trade.
While most brokerages backed Bagchi's appointment and said that it 'resolves leadership overhang', some analysts warned it would take time for him to settle in.
He would first need to rebuild the team, and over the longer term, he could bring fresh ideas and help ease governance concerns, Anand Dama, head BFSI analyst at Nuvama, told Reuters.
Bagchi, currently CEO at ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, had held senior roles at ICICI Bank, the country's second-biggest private lender, where he oversaw the retail and wholesale banking businesses. He also led ICICI Securities for six years.
At 56, he has a long runway to remain at the helm of HDFC Bank under Reserve Bank of India regulations, which cap a bank CEO's age at 70.
A key overhang surrounding the bank's leadership has been removed at a time when the firm is seeking to rebuild investor confidence, said Motilal Oswal. Bagchi's experience will be an asset, the brokerage said.
HDFC Bank on Saturday also posted a jump of around 18.8% in its deposits and a 16.3% rise in its gross advances as of September end.
"While the provisional data and appointment of an outsider CEO were positive, investors may be pricing in a period of clean-up and operational changes before growth accelerates. That could mean a few more quarters of pressure on the operational performance," Neeraj Dewan, an independent analyst, told Reuters.
HDFC Bank has so far underperformed peers after a 2023 merger with its parent weighed on its margins and growth. Chairman Atanu Chakraborty's abrupt March resignation over governance concerns further weighed on sentiments, even though an independent legal review did not substantiate his claims.
The stock now trades at a 25% discount to ICICI on a price-to-adjusted book value basis, and is down nearly 31% since it hit a record high in 2025.
Forty analysts rate HDFC Bank "buy" on average, with a median target price of Rs 972, as per data compiled by LSEG, implying a 37% upside for the stock.
Bagchi "has an opportunity to start with a relatively clean slate and reset both the narrative around the bank's performance and investor expectations," Bernstein analysts said in a note.
Brokerages are bullish on HDFC Bank's prospects on the appointment of Anup Bagchi as CEO.
Brokerages said the appointment is expected to serve HDFC well.
It allows the bank to optimise its operating structure and leadership team to better achieve growth, profitability and governance objectives, said Jefferies.
"Anup Bagchi's appointment provides clarity on management succession and strategic direction. Timely team changes could support execution," said Jefferies.
The global brokerage has a 'Buy' call on the stock with target price of Rs 880.
Attractive valuation at 1.4x FY28 adjusted P/B leaves scope for rerating, said Jefferies.
A key overhang surrounding the bank's leadership has been removed, noted Motilal Oswal, adding that Bagchi brought an external perspective at a time when the firm is seeking to rebuild investor confidence.
His experience across retail and wholesale banking, digital financial services, capital markets, wealth management and insurance will be an asset across HDFC's BFSI segments, the brokerage added.
Emkay Global said stability in upper management, reviving deposit growth and improving productivity of newer branches would be key priorities for the incoming CEO.

 Stock Market Today 
 Indian equities ended four-day losing streak on October 5.
 Sensex rose 472 points and Nifty closed above 22,500.
 Falling crude prices and buying across sectors supported markets.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Indian equity indices snapped their four-day losing streak on October 5, with the Nifty closing above 22,500 in a volatile session, supported by falling crude oil prices and buying across sectors, barring pharma and healthcare.
The market opened on a strong note amid positive global cues and the Nifty touched an intraday high of 22,621.80 in the initial hours. However, mid-session profit booking dragged the index to a low of 22,397.10. The benchmark staged a strong recovery in the second half of the session and closed comfortably above the 22,500 mark.
At close, the Sensex was up 472.77 points or 0.66 percent at 72,382.47, and the Nifty was up 133.80 points or 0.60 percent at 22,555.75.
Broader indices performed inline with benchmark indices, with the Nifty Midcap and Smallcap indices adding 0.5 percent each.
Also Read - MPC Poll: RBI likely to hike repo rate 25 bps as crude, global yields fuel inflation risks 
Biggest Nifty gainers were Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, ITC, Bajaj Finance, Shriram Finance, NTPC, while losers included HCL Technologies, Max Healthcare, HDFC Bank, Asian Paints and Apollo Hospitals.
Except pharma, all other sectoral indices ended in the green with Consumer Durables, FMCG, Media, Infra, Oil & Gas, PSU Bank, Telecom, Realty up 0.5-2 percent.
Also Read - Jane Street's likely SAT defence: Bank Nifty went the other way in over 90% of trading windows 
More than 200 stocks touched 52-week low, including UPL, Swan Corp, Bikaji Foods, Bombay Burmah, Medplus Health, JK Lakshmi Cem, Godawari Power, NBCC (India), IEX, Vedanta Aluminium, IndiaMART InterMESH, Motherson Sumi Wiring India, Trident, General Insurance Corporation of India, ABLBL, Bayer CropScience, Jyothy Labs, Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), IRFC and Godrej Consumer Products, among others. Among individual stocks, Raymond Realty shares gained 6% after reporting strong Q2 performance, while HDFC Bank shed 2% after the RBI approved Anup Bagchi’s appointment as MD & CEO. DLF gained nearly 1.4% after the complete sell-out of its luxury residential project in Gurugram.
TCS advanced 1.4% after announcing an agreement with Best Buy to transition its Global Capability Center in India to TCS. Avenue Supermarts shed over 6% after Citi maintained a ‘Sell’ rating with a target price of ₹3,300.
Also Read - Accenture Q4 beat boosts AI demand hopes; pricing pressure remains a worry for Indian IT 
PNB gained 2% despite an administrative warning issued by SEBI to its company secretary over insider trading regulation violations. Bajaj Finance jumped 2% after its board approved fundraising of up to ₹11,700 crore through QIP and ₹5,800 crore through preferential issue of warrants.
KPI Green Energy fell 6% after Group CEO Alok Das resigned, while Petronet LNG rose 1.3% after the board approved Sanjay Kumar’s appointment as MD & CEO. Poonawalla Fincorp gained 4.5% after reporting AUM of approximately ₹73,950 crore.

Runwal Enterprises shares ended mostly unchanged at ₹304.7 after making a flat market debut at ₹305 apiece on the NSE.
Orient Cables shares ended 48% higher at ₹403 after making a strong debut at ₹450, a premium of more than 65% over its IPO price.
AceVector shares finished 20% lower at ₹25.60 after a weak debut at ₹28.32, an 11% discount to its IPO price.
German Green Steel and Power shares ended 7.6% lower at ₹128.35 after listing at ₹143.50, around a 3% premium to its IPO price of ₹139.
 Ajit Mishra, SVP – research, Religare Broking

 Gold may rebound in 2027 if Fed's rate path becomes less aggressive: HSBC
 HSBC says gold could recalibrate higher next year if the pace of US rate hikes fails to match the market’s hawkish expectations.
 Khushi Keswani 
 October 05, 2026 / 12:40 IST 
 --> 
 Central banks could put a floor under gold even as near-term risks pile up: HSBC 
 Gold could recover if Fed's rate hikes are less aggressive.
 HSBC cuts near-term forecasts due to oil, dollar, and rates.
 Central bank buying and institutional demand support gold.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Gold could stage a recovery next year if the Federal Reserve’s rate path turns out less aggressive than markets currently expect, according to HSBC. The bank has cut its near-term forecasts after recent pressure from higher oil prices, a firm dollar and hawkish rate expectations, but it still sees scope for the metal to recalibrate higher in 2027.
HSBC’s chief precious metals analyst James Steel said gold has already been through a turbulent year. Prices touched a record $5,450 an ounce on 30 January before sliding to $3,942 by the end of June, as the Iran conflict, rising oil, higher yields and a stronger dollar triggered heavy liquidation. A late-summer recovery on returning investor interest faded once the Fed delivered its September rate hike and markets began pricing in further tightening.
Those same forces are expected to keep gold under pressure in the near term. Rising oil, a firm US dollar and expectations of additional rate increases have pushed the metal back on the defensive, and HSBC has lowered its forecasts to reflect the less favourable backdrop. Yet the bank is not abandoning its longer-term constructive stance. “Should the pace of rate hikes not meet the market’s hawkish expectations, gold may recalibrate higher,” Steel wrote.
One of the more durable supports, in HSBC’s view, is buying by central banks. Official sector purchases have remained steady, driven by long-term diversification policies and geopolitical concerns. The bank expects this demand to continue and help put a floor under prices even if speculative interest weakens.
Institutional demand for large bars has also held up reasonably well. HSBC points to regulatory changes in India and China that now allow financial institutions to buy more gold, alongside soft property and equity markets in both countries. At the same time, the heavy ETF selling seen earlier in the year is beginning to reverse as investors return to gold’s traditional role as a safe haven and portfolio diversifier.
Physical demand remains the weaker link. High prices have sharply reduced jewelry buying, and HSBC sees little chance of a quick recovery while inflation and tighter household incomes persist. Coin demand is similarly soft, though the bank suggests it may be nearing a bottom. If investor flows slow again, the combination of weak consumer demand and gradually rising supply could start to weigh more visibly on prices.
Supply itself is not expanding rapidly. Mine output is expected to rise in 2026 and 2027, but the increases look modest, constrained by falling ore grades and the difficulty of developing new projects. Recycling has so far been less responsive to high prices than in past cycles, although HSBC expects it to pick up later this year and into 2027.
Fiscal and geopolitical factors add another layer. Larger government deficits are negative for gold in the short run because they push yields higher. Over a longer horizon, HSBC sees them as potentially supportive because of the economic strain they can create. Geopolitical risks remain a background positive.
Near-term conditions look unfavourable. Rates, oil and the dollar are headwinds. But central bank buying, steadier institutional demand, especially from India and China, and the chance that the Fed may not deliver as many hikes as the market currently expects give the bank reason to stay constructive beyond the next few months.
 Khushi Keswani

docs.title: Blockbuster debut: Orient Cables shares list at 65% premium; should you buy, sell or hold?
docs.text: Orient Cables shares made a strong market debut at more than 65 percent premium over its initial public offering (IPO) price on Monday, following a 92.27 times subscription to its issue in the primary market between September 25 and 29.Shares of Orient Cables (India) were listed at Rs 450 per share on the NSE, a premium of 65.44 percent. The Rs 552-crore issue had a price band of Rs 258-272 per share.On the BSE, the shares of the company were listed at Rs 448.10 per share, a premium of 64.74 percent. The companys market capitalisation post listing of its shares stood at Rs 5,099.36-crore.Orient Cables market debut was better than expected in the grey market, which had anticipated a listing gain of about 40-45 percent.Check All IPO NewsEarlier, the company raised Rs 165.6 crore from anchor investors.Orient Cables share price listing today: Should you buy, sell or hold?Mahesh M.Ojha, Vice President Research and Business Development at Kantilal Chhaganlal Securities, said "Orient Cables offers a combination of strong market positioning, diversified product capabilities and robust revenue Growth, supported by rising demand from telecom, broadband, data centres, optical fibre, renewable energy and emerging applications such as EV charging. The Company ranks among India’s top four networking cable players with around 23 percent market share in FY26 and has established long-standing relationships with marquee customers. Revenue grew at a strong 33.5 percent CAGR during FY24–FY26, while FY26 RoNW stood at around 26 percent, reflecting healthy capital efficiency.He said, "The Company is further expanding its addressable market through optical fibre cables, passive networking products, specialty cables, harness assemblies and EV charging solutions. The fresh issue of Rs 320 crore includes Rs 155.5 crore towards repayment/prepayment of borrowings and Rs 91.5 crore towards capital expenditure, which should support balance-sheet strengthening and capacity expansion. The recently commissioned Bengaluru facility should also enhance the company’s ability to serve customers in South India. However, at the upper price band Rs 272, the issue is valued at around 51.6x PE FY26. Growth Investor who have long term horizon can Hold however Short Term Investor can book Partial Listing Gain."Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used for capital expenditure towards the purchase of machinery, equipment and civil works at its manufacturing facilities, besides repayment or partial prepayment of certain borrowings.A portion of the IPO funds will also be used for general corporate purposes.Orient Cables specialises in networking cables and passive networking equipment and caters to industries including broadband, telecom, data centres, renewable energy and smart building automation.Its product portfolio is divided into three broad segments – networking cables and solutions, speciality power and optical fibre cables and solutions and other allied products.Disclaimer: The views and investment tips expressed by investment experts on Moneycontrol.com are their own and not those of the website or its management. Markets 
 Stock recommendations for 6 October from MarketSmith India
 MarketSmith India 6 min read 6 Oct 2026, 06:00 AM IST 
 Summary
 MarketSmith India reveals its top stock recommendations for today, 6 October. Get expert insights into the best-performing stocks to guide your investment decisions. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Stock-market recap: Indian equities closed higher today as positive global cues, bargain hunting after eight weekly declines, and easing crude oil prices improved risk appetite.
 Softer-than-expected US employment data reduced expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike, supporting Asian markets and encouraging buying. Strong gains in heavyweight consumer and financial stocks helped the Nifty reclaim 22,500, while DII purchases provided support against continued FII selling. Improved market breadth, with 32 Nifty stocks advancing against 18 declines, indicated participation in the recovery.
 However, not every sector closed in the green: Pharma (-0.74%) and Healthcare (-1.00%) declined, while IT finished flat (0.00%). Despite today’s rebound, elevated crude prices, high US bond yields, rupee weakness, and persistent foreign outflows remain near-term risks for investor sentiment.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India:

 Stock recommendations for 5 October from MarketSmith India
 MarketSmith India 12 min read 5 Oct 2026, 06:01 AM IST 
 Summary
 MarketSmith India reveals its top stock recommendations for today, 5 October. Get expert insights into the best-performing stocks to guide your investment decisions.

 Stock market recap: Indian equities fell for a fourth straight session on Thursday, while the market posted its eighth consecutive weekly loss, its longest such losing streak since 2001.
 The Nifty 50 fell 198.50 points, or 0.88%, to close at 22,421.95, its lowest level since April, after hitting an intraday low of 22,217.30. The Sensex lost 570.59 points, or 0.79%, to settle at 71,909.70. The Nifty fell about 3.1% during the holiday-shortened week.
 A rebound in crude oil prices, higher US bond yields and a rupee that weakened past 96 to the dollar added to the pressure.
 Auto stocks were hit hardest after weak September sales, with Bajaj Auto falling about 8%. Maruti, M&M, and Eicher Motors also declined. Hospital stocks, including Apollo Hospitals and Max Healthcare, extended losses amid concerns over drug-price controls. Metals and FMCG stocks were also weak.
 IT stocks and Kotak Mahindra Bank provided some support. Kotak Mahindra Bank rose about 3% after naming a new chief executive.
 Market breadth was negative, with 1,023 stocks advancing, 2,574 declining and 110 unchanged. Indian stock markets will remain shut on Friday, and the Reserve Bank of India’s policy decision is the next key event markets will wait for.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: GNG Electronics Ltd (current price: ₹ 705) 
 Why it’s recommended: India’s largest organized refurbished ICT device player, benefiting from rising demand for affordable and sustainable laptops/desktops along with strong global presence across multiple countries. An integrated sourcing-refurbishment-distribution model, expanding enterprise partnerships, and increasing acceptance of refurbished devices support scalable revenue growth and margin expansion. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 54.97, 52-week high: ₹ 730.00, volume: ₹ 61.47 crore 
 Technical analysis: Trendline Breakout 
 Risk factors: Business is highly dependent on the availability of used IT assets and procurement relationships; any disruption in sourcing can impact volumes and profitability. Intense competition from new-device manufacturers and other refurbishers, along with technology obsolescence, could pressure margins and demand. 
 Buy: ₹ 698–709 
 Target price: ₹ 820 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 666 
 Buy: Paisalo Digital Ltd (current price: ₹ 80) 
 Why it’s recommended: Strong co-lending partnerships with banks and a technology-driven lending platform enable rapid AUM growth while expanding financial inclusion in underserved rural and semi-urban markets. Large customer base, improving geographic reach, and scalable business correspondent model provide a long runway for credit growth.
 Key metrics: P/E: 27.72, 52-week high: ₹ 94.88, volume: ₹ 123.23 crore 
 Technical analysis: Bounce back from its 50-DMA 
 Risk factors: Exposure to economically vulnerable borrowers makes asset quality sensitive to rural income stress, economic slowdowns, and challenges of collection. Regulatory changes affecting NBFCs, co-lending frameworks, interest rates, or digital lending practices could impact growth and profitability. 
 Buy at: ₹ 79–80 
 Target price: ₹ 90 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 76 
 How Nifty 50 performed 
 On 1 October, Indian equities ended sharply lower, although a late-session recovery helped the benchmark indices close well above their intraday lows. The Nifty 50 fell 198.50 points, or 0.88%, to 22,421.95 after hitting an intraday low of 22,217.30, while the Sensex ended around 71,910, down about 570 points.
 Market breadth remained distinctly weak. Exchange-wide data at 4 pm showed 1,023 stocks advancing, against 2,574 declining and 110 unchanged. This translates to an advance-decline ratio of roughly 0.40, pointing to broad-based selling beyond the headline indices.
 On the sectoral front, IT was the clearest outperformer, rising 2.17%, while private banks were broadly flat. Auto (-3.46%), Metal (-2.35%), Media (-2.33%), Consumer Durables (-1.91%) and FMCG (-1.61%) led the declines. Persistent foreign institutional selling, elevated US bond yields and volatility in crude oil prices weighed on sentiment.
 The Nifty 50 remains firmly in a bearish price structure, extending its sequence of lower highs and lower lows. The index has decisively broken below the horizontal consolidation structure visible on the daily chart and continues to trade below all major moving averages, reinforcing the prevailing downtrend. The earlier rising trendline has also been breached, with subsequent price action failing to reclaim it, pointing to a deterioration in the medium-term trend.
 Momentum indicators remain weak. The RSI has fallen to around 22.6, deep in oversold territory and below its signal average, highlighting intense negative momentum. This raises the possibility of a short-term mean-reversion move, but does not by itself confirm a trend reversal. The MACD remains below both its signal line and the zero line, while the negative histogram persists, confirming that bearish momentum remains dominant.
 The Nifty 50 registered a fresh low near 22,200 before recovering part of its intraday losses. On the downside, 22,200–22,000 remains a key support zone. A sustained break below this band could intensify selling pressure and potentially extend the decline towards 21,700–21,600. Conversely, any near-term recovery is likely to face initial resistance at 22,600–22,800, which has emerged as a key technical hurdle following the recent breakdown.
 How did the Nifty Bank perform? 
 Nifty Bank opened on a negative note at 54,583.

docs.title: IPO mutual funds: How do fund managers buy and sell shares at pre- and post-listing stages? Experts explain
docs.text:
Examples include Edelweiss Recently Listed IPO Fund and Mirae Asset BSE Select IPO ETF FoF. While one is an active fund that gives the fund manager flexibility to select stocks, the other is a passive fund that tracks an index. But how do fund managers actually buy and sell IPO stocks, and what should investors look at when evaluating these funds? Uttam Agarwal, Chief Business Officer at Bajaj Capital, mentioned that “for a fund manager, the real work starts much before the listing. Fund managers study the offer documents, meet the management and look at the business, financials, promoter track record and, importantly, whether the valuation makes sense”. Once they decide to invest, position sizing becomes important. With a newly listed company, there is limited market history, so a manager may start with a measured allocation and increase it as the business delivers and the investment case gets stronger. The same thinking applies to exits. A stock going up isn't automatically a reason to sell. If the business continues to perform and the valuation remains reasonable, there may be merit in staying invested. If the fundamentals or valuation change, the manager can reassess, he explained. Manish P. Hingar, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Fintoo, explained that the IPO-focused mutual funds can buy IPO shares at different stages: “Buying shares from unlisted markets before the IPO is launched doesn't apply here since it is a different type of investment activity,” Piyush Jhunjhunwala, Founder and CEO, Stockify, added. An exit from a position will not typically be dictated simply by financial results. The fund manager will continue tracking the stock's valuation, the prospects for its earnings, its cash flows, the way it operates, its competition, and its corporate developments, Jhunjhunwala added. A stock may be sold even after strong returns if its valuation runs ahead of expected earnings growth. Weakening business prospects, poor earnings visibility, governance concerns, or a change in the investment thesis can also prompt an exit, he added. “Portfolio turnover will depend on the investment philosophy of the fund and the current market environment. However, high turnover in itself cannot be seen as a positive,” Jhunjhunwala noted. The mainboard is likely to remain the larger opportunity set for most IPO-focused strategies because these companies generally offer greater scale, disclosure, and liquidity. Whether a particular fund can invest in SME IPOs depends on its mandate, Agarwal mentioned. An IPO fund is better viewed as a small addition to an equity portfolio rather than a core holding. Investors should look beyond returns and popular IPOs and check the portfolio’s sector exposure, number of holdings, allocation to newly listed stocks, valuations and concentration, Hingar said. Investors should also assess whether the portfolio reflects the fund’s stated strategy, including its market-cap and recent-listing exposure. Don't judge portfolio based on listing day gains, Agarwal said. Expense ratio, portfolio turnover ratio, downside risk and consistency of returns are also useful indicators. Investors should also check how much of the fund is actually invested in newly listed and IPO companies, Jhunjhunwala added. Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only. On the rationale behind being bullish on Chalet Hotels shares, the Jefferies India report says, “We hosted Chalet's senior management for meetings in SG. Key takeaways include visibility on strong growth over the next 5 yrs, driven by its existing pipeline (~9-10% keys CAGR) & potential new adds/M&A. Management aims to build Athiva into a leading pan-India premium hospitality brand (1,200-1,500 keys). Co targets higher leisure mix & selective market expansion, while its high-margin CRE portfolio provides recurring CFs that underpin growth & earnings stability.” The Jefferies India report further added that management's vision extends beyond adding room inventory, focusing instead on building a scaled owner-operator ecosystem through large-format asset ownership, selective geographic expansion, growth of its owned brand Athiva, & increased use of franchise-led models. Partnerships such as Marriott's Autograph Collection & IHCL's first Taj franchise with Chalet underscore its rising operating credibility, while stable annuity income from commercial RE provides the capital flexibility to fund future growth. The global brokerage said that management outlined its rapid growth plans, supported by its 2,036-key development pipeline (including recent additions in Pune & Hyderabad totalling ~380 keys). Growth is expected to be largely execution-led, with existing assets contributing half of the EBITDA growth over the next 5 years, driven by LFL growth and asset sweating and the other half through new projects/ acquisitions. Management expects RevPAR growth in mid-to-high single digits, supporting overall revenue growth in the mid-teens. The Chalet Hotels' management continues to expand beyond its traditional Western India concentration but remains disciplined in market selection. Recent additions in Aravali, the Himalayas & Udaipur, alongside the upcoming Taj property at Delhi Airport, reflect a conscious effort to build a stronger presence in Northern India. Near-term additions include the phased opening of Taj Delhi Airport (starting with ~70 rooms) and Athiva South Goa over the next 18-24 months, following approvals which are expected by Jan-27. Chalet Hotels' commercial RE portfolio is a key pillar of its growth strategy, generating ~Rs2.5-3bn of annual EBITDA. These recurring CFs provide a stable earnings base, strengthen debt serviceability and support future expansion in Hotels, reducing dependence on the inherently cyclical hotel business. Giving a ‘buy’ rating to Chalet Hotels shares, the Jefferies India report said, “Buy rated with a PT (Price Target) of ₹ 965 (SOTP-based)." However, the brokerage warned investors, highlighting some key risks, which are as follows: 1] A slowdown in the global/domestic economy; 2] Resurfacing of issues such as a pandemic, and 3] Magnified impact of downcycle, given 100% Asset Owner model.  The surge in rates is blowing up commercial real-estate deals
 Peter Grant , The Wall Street Journal 4 min read 6 Oct 2026, 06:22 AM IST 
 Summary
 Property buyers are demanding sellers renegotiate terms because of higher mortgage rates, signaling broader market distress. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 A growing number of commercial real-estate buyers are threatening to walk away from recent transactions unless the seller offers better terms.
 Rapidly rising interest rates are to blame.
 Investors who agreed to a purchase price earlier this year when financing was cheaper are now demanding price cuts or other concessions before closing.
 That insistence on retrading deals began when bond yields started to rise in late summer. It intensified last month after the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point and signaled more to come.
 “Rates went up, what, just a few days ago and I’m already getting calls where they’re talking retrade,” Jeff Powers, a Cushman & Wakefield managing director, said last month.
 The typical six to 12 months between when a buyer signs a contract and when the sale is completed can make a substantial difference in financing costs when borrowing rates are rising as rapidly as they are now.
 Eastham Capital agreed to pay about $20 million for a roughly 200-unit apartment property in the Midwest. Before it put down a deposit, borrowing costs jumped by more than six-tenths of a percentage point, said Matt Rosenthal, the Boca Raton, Fla.-based firm’s founder and managing director.
 Rosenthal was able to convince the seller to cut the price by $600,000, after threatening to walk away. “It’s certainly a different deal now,” he said.
 These retrades are an early sign of broader market distress weighing on property values, slowing development and making maturing loans harder to refinance.
 “We are working harder to close deals now than we ever have before,” said Bobby Werhane, a managing director of Marcus & Millichap’s IPA Capital Markets division.
 Commercial real estate—from offices in certain cities to shopping malls and hotels—had been enjoying a budding recovery. Reduced new supply, a pickup in workers returning to the office and a leveling off in interest rates in recent years helped boost property values.
 Now, the sudden surge in interest rates is derailing that period of progress.
 The fallout extends beyond property owners. Falling real-estate values and fewer sales squeeze property-tax and transfer-tax collections. Higher rates also make it harder for developers to earn their targeted returns. That cuts demand for construction workers, architects and building materials.
 “The hurdle is simply higher,” said Alfonso Munk, co-head of investment management at Houston-based Hines, one of the country’s largest developers.
 Few industries are as sensitive to interest rates as commercial real estate. Buyers typically put up only a fraction of a property’s purchase price and borrow the rest, boosting the return on their invested money.
 More than $5 trillion of commercial and multifamily real-estate mortgages are outstanding. That is far more than Americans owe on credit cards or auto loans combined.
 Earlier this year, commercial real-estate investors were expecting the Fed to cut rates. Property values were increasing because debt was costing less and yields on competing investments such as bonds were dropping, making commercial real estate more attractive.
 Now the mood has soured as rising rates have driven values down. From late August, when rates began rising more sharply, through Friday, the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs Index fell more than 8%, while the S&P 500 gained 1%, according to real-estate analytics firm Green Street.
 Higher rates are also adding to landlord distress because mortgages made when borrowing costs were lower come due. Owners that can’t refinance or repay the loans at maturity are falling behind or being pushed into special servicing.
 Data firm Trepp reported that in August, 11.42% of mortgages packaged into commercial mortgage-backed securities were being handled by special servicers, a sign that those loans were facing problems such as missed payments or difficulty refinancing at maturity. That is the highest special-servicing rate since February 2013.
 One bright spot is that lenders and investment funds still have ample capital to put to work. Debt and equity investors have raised money faster than the market has produced deals, intensifying competition among lenders for the strongest projects.
 Northwind Group, a New York-based lender, recently provided a $208 million first mortgage to convert much of a 355,000-square-foot office tower in Brooklyn into apartments. Ran Eliasaf, Northwind’s founder and managing partner, said banks and private lenders competed heavily to make the loan.
 Eliasaf agreed that higher rates have increased loan pricing and prompted more conservative property valuations. But the increase “hasn’t changed the ability for borrowers to obtain loans,” he said. “It’s a very deep, liquid market right now.”
 Still, on the front lines, fights over price and retrade attempts are becoming more common.
 In June, real-estate firm Medalist Diversified agreed to sell a 65,000-square-foot retail property in Greenville, S.C., for about $10.2 million. As rates rose during the summer, the buyer sought a price cut.
 After a period of wrangling, Medalist agreed to reduce the price by $100,000, and the deal closed in September “due to the potential impact of the interest rate environment,” said Chief Financial Officer C. Brent Winn Jr.
 And some lenders are backing out. A bank participating in a $45 million construction loan for a more than 90%-leased retail center in North Carolina pulled out because of market conditions. Marcus & Millichap was able to find a replacement lender.

docs.text:

 All B-1 bombers returning to US from UK base
 Shelby Holliday , Michael R. Gordon , Max Colchester , The Wall Street Journal 2 min read 5 Oct 2026, 06:15 AM IST 
 Summary
 The withdrawal came amid security concerns around the base where six suspects were arrested last week in connection to a suspected plot. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 The U.S. removed all its B-1 bombers from the U.K.’s RAF Fairford air base, a decision stemming from security concerns over suspected terror plots against the facility, American officials said Sunday.
 The decision represents a shift for the U.S. which has used the military base, northwest of London, as a hub for launching bomber strikes in Iran. Until their recent departure, a dozen B-1s had been stationed at the base.
 “While operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time, we can acknowledge now that all U.S. bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have redeployed to their home stations in the United States,” the Pentagon said in a statement, adding that the bombers remained ready to deliver global strike capabilities from the continental U.S. The U.K. Ministry of Defense declined to comment.
 The decision follows the arrest of six suspects in connection to a suspected attack on the base that U.S. and British official said was foiled last Sunday. U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were “strong indications” that Iran played a role in the incident, which was shrouded in mystery after the U.K. released the suspects on bail but continued to investigate the situation.
 U.S. officials were aware of an Iran-linked plot to attack the bomber aircraft and kill personnel at the base, The Wall Street Journal has reported. A branch of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps had recruited U.K. nationals to carry out the plot, which involved multiple steps including a diversion in the neighborhood nearby, according to a senior U.S. official.
 In the U.K., authorities are still trying to piece together what happened, and some U.K. officials question the level of sophistication of the planned attack.

docs.title: NPS Swasthya: How the new healthcare savings model works
